references.text: The Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron and accused God of bringing them out of Egypt to die, reflecting the same complaining attitude and accusation of God's hatred.
The spies who returned spread bad reports and caused the people to grumble against the Lord, which is the background for the accusation in Deuteronomy.
The Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness and accused them of bringing them out to die, an early example of the people's pattern of complaining.
The psalmist describes how the Israelites grumbled in their tents and did not obey the Lord's voice, a direct reference to this event.
The people spoke against God and Moses and asked why they were brought out of Egypt, a recurring theme of complaint and accusation.
The people grumbled against Moses and accused him of bringing them out of Egypt to kill them, showing the same pattern of distrust.
Paul warns against grumbling as some of the Israelites did and were killed by the destroyer, a New Testament reference to the Israelites' grumbling in the wilderness.
